title: Prune Microshift Retreat - Nov 2026
content:
Context: Quick internal 'microshift' grooming retreat: 3 half-days (Oct 26-28) focused on pruning console backlog ahead of sprint-42 planning. Goal was to reduce WIP, identify canary and must-have items for next two sprints, and produce a short, actionable cutlist (the 'sniper' list) for on-call and PM alignment.

Attendees: Maya Chen (lead), Rafael Ortiz (PM), Priya Nair (UX), Samir Gupta (SRE), Leah Kim (Analytics), plus ad-hoc input from infra and devexp.

High-level goals for the retreat:
- Remove / defer low-impact console tickets that block rollout cadence
- Identify 4 must-have items that unblock Dedicated rollout telemetry
- Define lightweight acceptance for each prioritized ticket (A/C + quick wireframe or CTA)
- Clarify cross-team deps and owners for each cut

Retreat framing and heuristics (how we triaged):
1) User impact priority > engineering nicety. If a ticket affects onboarding, billing routes, or rollout visibility -> bump.
2) Cost of delay: >7d impact to sales/enterprise -> prioritize.
3) Risk to platform stability or customer SLA -> must-have rollback/fallback plan before merge.
4) Acceptable defer window: OK to defer items with no immediate rollout dependency for 2 sprints.
5) If ticket requires infra changes (INF- prefixed), pair with infra owner and create explicit rollback plan.

Decisions made (summary):
- Must-have for sprint-42: observability drilldown for per-route latency (INF-4299), canary rollback button in console, and route-level quota visualization.
- Defer to sprint-43: bulk-route-migration wizard (too many deps), advanced RBAC role matrix (enterprise sales tie but high effort).
- Cancel / archive: old prototyping wireframes for 'theme editor' (low product signal).

Sniper cutlist (final prioritized items):
1) CON-1987 | Route latency drilldown (must-have)
   - Rationale: Blocks Dedicated SLA verification for top 5 customers.
   - Owner: Leah Kim (analytics), Eng lead: Samir
   - Estimate: 5d dev + 2d QA
   - Acceptance: per-route 95th/50th latency panel, link to trace, flag for auto-fallback when >Xms.
   - Dependencies: INF-4299 (metrics ingestion), instrument endpoint.

2) CON-2042 | Canary rollback control (must-have)
   - Rationale: Operational safety for canary deploys; essential for canary A/B rollout policy.
   - Owner: Rafael Ortiz (PM), Eng: Rafael + DevExp
   - Estimate: 3d dev + 1d UX polish
   - Acceptance: single-click rollback on rollout page, confirm modal, audit log entry. GitHub PR must include e2e that exercises rollback path.

3) CON-2120 | Route quotas visualization (high-priority)
   - Rationale: Sales asks for quota clarity; reduces support tickets ~20% in trials.
   - Owner: Maya Chen
   - Estimate: 4d
   - Acceptance: per-route quota bar, warnings when usage >80%, link to quota increase flow.

4) CON-2175 | Lightweight intake filter for console backlog (nice-to-have)
   - Rationale: Reduces noisy incoming tickets and straightens triage.
   - Owner: Priya Nair
   - Estimate: 2d prototype.
   - Acceptance: UI wireframe + two sample ticket flows; incremental rollout to internal only.

5) INF-4312 | Metric sampling adjustment (infra dependency) (must do before CON-1987)
   - Rationale: Current sampling skips 95th percentile on low-volume routes.
   - Owner: Infra oncall
   - Estimate: 3d

Tickets deferred or archived:
- CON-1801 (theme editor) -> archive (low signal)
- CON-2009 (bulk route migration wizard) -> defer to sprint-43 (dependency-laden)
- CON-1734 (legacy toolbar cleanup) -> defer to backlog hygiene cycle Q1 2027

Wireframe notes (quick sketches / UX calls):
- Rollout page micro-interaction: place rollback button top-right next to 'promote' CTA. Use danger-confirmation with typed input 'ROLLBACK'. Keep animation minimal to avoid accidental double-clicks.
- Latency panel: stacked bars for p50/p95 + a small sparkline. Hover reveals link to trace ID; clicking opens trace in a side panel with action 'trigger auto-fallback' if enabled.
- Quota visualization: compact horizontal bars with color stop at 80% and 100%. Clicking should surface 'request increase' modal pre-populated with route id and tier.

Telemetry / observability gating checklist (required before any canary rollouts):
- [ ] Metrics ingestion confirmed for 95th pctl (INF-4312)
- [ ] Alert rule for route latency > threshold for 5m
- [ ] Audit logs capture rollout action and rollback action
- [ ] Synthetic canary traffic test in staging runs successfully

Open questions and risks (to resolve before merge):
- How to surface quota changes to users on mobile vs web (Priya to propose mobile fallback).
- Do we allow self-service quota increases for enterprise or require sales approval? (Sales input required: SLS-290)
- Rollback DB migration risk for routes using pinned model versions — need infra sign-off.

Next steps and owners (by Nov 9):
- Leah: spike INF-4299 integration and confirm metrics with infra (due Nov 4).
- Samir: prototype rollback API and propose safety checklist (due Nov 6).
- Priya: produce mobile-friendly wireframe for quota panel (due Nov 7).
- PMs: update Jira tickets with A/C and link to this doc (Maya to audit).

Notes to self / informal fragments from the retreat:
- "sniper" list should be minimal but end-to-end (UI, API, metrics) 
- Keep UX copy short for rollback confirmations; legal wants an audit mention.
- Consider feature-flag gating for rollback until 2 weeks post-launch.

Historical context pulled in: follow-up from Route Decision Lattice workshop (see linked Confluence). This doc is intentionally tactical: reduce noise and create a runnable plan for next two sprints.

If you disagree with any cut or classification, comment directly in the Jira ticket and ping the retreat thread in Slack (linked_artifacts above).
